title: Rocket Report: Artemis II literally tore through the atmosphere; New Glenn delay
gist: Quilty Space projects a shortfall of about 150 launches outside China through 2030 that may last into the late 2030s. Blue Origin delayed New Glenn's return to flight to January 2027 and unveiled the Northstar engine (25% of BE-4 cost) and a hydrogen kick stage. China detailed its pre-2030 crewed lunar landing roadmap, and a study found Artemis II disturbed the ionosphere more than any launch to date.

insights.claim: Quilty Space estimates that outside China there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches versus demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies between now and 2030.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Launch scarcity gives pricing power to SpaceX and any new entrant that reaches reliable cadence, and slows constellation deployments.

insights.claim: If US military launch demand is included and SpaceX does not extend Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy for national security needs, the Western launch shortage through 2030 could double to roughly 300 launches.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: National security launch needs could crowd out commercial customers, which strengthens SpaceX's negotiating position.

insights.claim: Quilty Space's Caleb Henry says the launch crisis is more severe than expected, will not end this decade, and may not abate until the late 2030s.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Launch supply constraints may last for years, which supports valuations of launch providers that are close to operating.
insights.quote: “What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s.”

insights.claim: Quilty attributes the launch shortage to Russian rockets leaving the Western market due to the Ukraine war, Amazon Leo demand, development delays of New Glenn, Vulcan, Neutron, Terran R and Nova, and Falcon 9's retirement from commercial service.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Every new rocket that slips makes the shortage worse, so first flights and cadence milestones for these vehicles matter a lot for the sector.

themes.theme: Blue Origin New Glenn cost-down and delay

insights.claim: Blue Origin's new Northstar engine, intended to replace the BE-4 on New Glenn's first stage, has half the parts, 30 percent less mass, about 65 percent 3D-printable content, more thrust, and an expected manufacturing cost of 25 percent of a BE-4.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A 75% cut in engine cost would change New Glenn's economics and make it more competitive with SpaceX.

insights.claim: Blue Origin aims to eventually position New Glenn to launch more than 1,000 times a year, with upgrades that reduce manufacturing cost and expand payload capacity to geostationary orbit and the Moon.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Shows how big Blue Origin's ambitions are, though it is far from its current cadence.

insights.claim: Blue Origin is developing a hydrogen-oxygen third stage for New Glenn with a lightweight composite tank, after completing its first composite liquid hydrogen tanking test at Launch Site One in Texas.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A high-energy kick stage puts New Glenn in competition for lunar and GEO missions.

insights.claim: Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp told employees New Glenn's return to flight is now targeted for January 2027 rather than December, following a destructive launch pad explosion at Cape Canaveral in May 2026.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: The delay is small, but it holds back NASA, Amazon, and Space Force payloads that are waiting on New Glenn.
insights.locator: New Glenn won’t return to flight

insights.claim: After its return to flight, New Glenn's manifest includes a spring 2027 launch of Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 lander, an uncrewed precursor to its human-rated lander for NASA's Artemis missions.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Blue Moon Mark 1 is a key milestone for Blue Origin's lunar lander contract.

insights.claim: China plans a crewed lunar landing before 2030 using separate launches of the Mengzhou crew ship and Lanyue lander on Long March 10 rockets, with a Long March 10A test in early 2027 and an uncrewed Lanyue lunar test in 2028.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A clear Chinese timeline adds geopolitical pressure on NASA's Artemis schedule and budget.
insights.locator: China reveals roadmap to lunar landing

insights.claim: China's SpaceSail (Qianfan) internet constellation has reached about 275 satellites since August 2024, toward a first phase of 1,296, with the latest 18 launched on CAS Space's Kinetica 2.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: China's progress on a Starlink competitor is slow but steady, and it matters in emerging markets.

insights.claim: CAS Space's Kinetica 2 uses three side-by-side boosters like a small Falcon Heavy, lifts about 12 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, and is intended to eventually have reusable boosters.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Chinese commercial launch startups are adding capacity that Western launch supply lacks.

themes.theme: New space startups and national programs

insights.claim: Argo Space, founded in 2022 by three former SpaceX Carlisle brothers, builds satellites that carry water and split it into hydrogen and oxygen with solar power for thrust; its first mission in July failed due to a solar array issue, and two demo missions are planned for 2027.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Water-based propulsion could enable in-space refueling from lunar resources, an early-stage infrastructure bet.
insights.locator: SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion

insights.claim: JAXA selected Interstellar Technologies for a government program granting up to $76 million per company to private launchers; Interstellar has raised over $250 million and targets a 2027 first launch of its 1-metric-ton Zero rocket.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Japan is funding a domestic commercial launch sector, which adds small-launch competition.

insights.claim: India's GSLV launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite carrying multiple atomic clocks of different designs to fix reliability problems after older navigation satellites suffered clock failures; GSLV has had 6 failures in 20 flights since 2001.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: India is working to rebuild a sovereign navigation system, one of several countries moving away from relying on GPS.

themes.theme: Launch effects on ionosphere and GPS

insights.claim: A National Cheng Kung University study found that NASA's Artemis II SLS launch caused ionospheric disturbances that could have triggered temporary localized GPS errors, up to 10 times more intense than those from SpaceX Starship tests despite Starship having twice the liftoff thrust.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: As launch cadence rises, effects on the ionosphere could become a regulatory or GNSS reliability issue.
insights.locator: Artemis II tore through the atmosphere
